title: Housing affordability and institutional financialization
framing: Housing costs have reached historic highs relative to income across most U.S. metros. Institutional investors now own significant shares of single-family homes in multiple markets. Algorithmic rent-setting software faces antitrust lawsuits. Multiple legislative efforts to address the crisis have stalled.
prompt: Housing affordability crisis deepens as institutional investors expand single-family home purchases.

goodFaith.text: It's a market design problem with market design solutions. Pass the bill.

coalition.text: Three versions of the same bill died. I still believe in legislation. Barely.

badFaith.text: Every legislator who votes no is running interference for private equity.

goodFaith.text: Upzone, reform permitting, build more. Corporate buyers fill a supply vacuum.

coalition.text: Supply is most of the answer. Algorithmic rent collusion is the rest.

badFaith.text: Deregulate construction. The market solves it. Blackstone didn't cause this.

goodFaith.text: Community land trusts work. Tenant unions work. Legislation is a supplement.

coalition.text: 'Protect the neighborhood' is starting to sound like NIMBY with better politics.

badFaith.text: There is no reform. The legislature is the landlord's instrument.

goodFaith.text: A small landlord is a neighbor. Invitation Homes is a spreadsheet.

coalition.text: The free-market argument I used is now being used against me.

badFaith.text: They outbid every family with cash. Zone them out. Tax them into selling.

LF.text: The left is naming a structural design problem — financialization of housing is a documented architecture with documented policy remedies, blocked by lobbying not by complexity.

LC.text: The left is watching three versions of the same bill die in committee and recognizing that belief in the legislative path is also belief in the institutions that keep deciding not to use it.

LD.text: The left is reading every market participant as private equity, treating rent itself as illegitimate income and any reformist position as complicity in dispossession.

RF.text: The right is correct that supply constraints are the foundational driver — fifty years of exclusion zoning created the vacuum institutional buyers walked into.

RC.text: The right is watching Delaware LLCs outbid families in cash and recognizing that the property-rights framework it used to protect community is now being used to tell it to shut up about the loss.

RD.text: The right is invoking "free market" to defend an arrangement where institutional capital faces none of the friction ordinary buyers face, scapegoating zoning to keep the rent-extraction architecture intact.
